result:
**Verdict: PASS** for DG6 round 11, candidate `c45d73b8` (source commit `33db1a46`). I raised one new finding, F-DG6-740, which is Low and not blocking.

I confirmed the candidate ID in the repository and in a disposable clone (2,769 files, nothing missing). HEAD adds only the freeze and assignment commit. I had no open findings from earlier rounds, so the verifications file holds an empty list.

**What ran, all in disposable clones:**

| Area | Result |
|---|---|
| Build, typecheck, lint, OpenAPI lint (932 operations), no-CDN, format, contrast | All exit 0 |
| Unit tests, Node 24.21.0 and 22.22.0, locale unset and C.UTF-8 | Pass |
| Integration, twice, each on a fresh database (119 migrations, 0001–0127) | Run 2: 441/441 files. 932/932 operations validated, 0 pending |
| `tests/qa` alone | 45 files, 437 tests |
| Product e2e, en and ar, both locales | 556 passed each time |
| Root acceptance specs (22), en and ar, both locales | 288 passed each time |
| Demo stack, en and ar, both locales | 30 passed each time |
| My probes, both languages, both locales | Pass: read-only auditor, 360/390 px and 200 % text, axe, XSS, browser storage, row counts, Arabic export literals |
| A13 kill/restart drills and the D-203 batch tests | Pass |
| Load and export (provisional, one sandbox host) | p95: reads 21 ms, updates 33 ms, dashboards 45 ms, export start 40 ms |
| Gate validator: historical DG5–DG1, register DG6, pipeline | All PASS |

**Skips:**
- The 18 skipped root tests are the routes the axe spec leaves unscanned by design, as the register notes disclose.
- The 2 skipped product tests need the demo database. They pass on the demo stack.

**Round-10 repair (BE-Z15, the issuer-tag tokens).** My 23-case API probe passes:
- A token copied from another rule, or from the published version into its draft, is refused as stale, and nothing changes.
- The new per-row key appears in no response, header, audit row or outbox payload, and it cannot be changed.
- Eight concurrent saves give one 200 and seven 409s.

Five mutants that undo the repairs are each caught, by both my probe and the candidate's own tests:

| Mutant | Failures |
|---|---|
| Z1 | 6 |
| Z2 | 15 |
| M2 | 31 |
| W1 | 2 |
| L1 | 10 |

**Open questions (D-234).** I found no served path that names a sensitive record, and no edit, grant-change or concurrent-save sequence that loses or misplaces a hidden value. The D-229 and D-228 (4) rulings hold.

**Failures I saw, each explained and passing when re-run:**
- One unit test file failed on both Node versions because my sparse clone left out a handback file it reads. It passes once the folder is added.
- A Vitest worker timeout under load on Node 22. The full re-run is clean.
- One contract test timed out at 30 s under load. Re-run alone: 218/218.
- My own run-order mistake made the exception probe fail in run 70. In the right order it passes (runs 70b and 71).
- My probe's P19 update failed in run 20 because it didn't bump the version. Fixed in 20b, 23/23.
- The export proof exits 1 only on the known LOAD-T20 dataset gap ("no sameScopeOther user"). That gap is already disclosed in the register notes.

**New finding: F-DG6-740 (Low, not mandatory, owner frontend-ux-engineer).** If an author pastes a token from another rule into the rule editor, the save is correctly refused and nothing is stored. But the screen then says "This rule changed after you opened it" in both English and Arabic, which is false here. The form reload also drops the author's other unsaved edits. The corrected problem text from the repair never appears in the editor. No hidden value is lost, swapped or disclosed. The candidate's own web test expects this message, so it is the behaviour as built rather than a regression.

**Assignment drifts:**
- I used `round: 11` instead of the assignment's `round: 7`, to match the round folder, as round 10 did.
- Node 22.22.2 isn't installed, so the Node 22 runs used 22.22.0.
- Migrations now end at 0127, not 0125.

**Environment residuals (PASS on the offline surface):** no live Keycloak login (no container runtime), no live registry or CI, and no real Mobily systems. The load figures are provisional engineering measurements, not Mobily capacity.

Files are in `docs/delivery/reviews/DG6/round-11/`:
- `qa-verifier.json`
- `qa-verifier.md`
- `qa-verifier.verifications.json`
- `qa-verifier.findings.json`

Evidence is in `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG6/qa/round-11/`, and my tests are in `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG6/qa/tests/round-11/`. The disposable clones and test scratch are removed.
